scope: Challenge input-only video gap-filling trial on top of the contact-carry working default. Tracking, tactical video and supplied homography only; no challenge labels, public-window scores, human video review or per-gap choices. Plan reviewed adversarially before implementation.

kill_test.design: Masked tracking-observed live windows with real-gap lengths; half 1 development (57 windows, 17,704 frames), half 2 frozen test (59 windows, 16,569 frames). Reference is hidden tracking (tracking agreement, not truth). Parameters fixed before results; no tuning.
kill_test.pass_rule: local search beats linear interpolation on the same covered frames by >= 5 points at 1.5 m, also after reweighting to real-gap confidence bins and in the onset-near-player stratum

real_gap_behaviour.interpretation: Real-gap fills are consistent but mostly short extensions near gap edges; gap interiors are not reconstructed.

self_trained_detector_round1.labels: First-half tracking-observed live frames (every 4th, ball speed < 25 m/s, development windows +-125 frames excluded) projected through the homography; 4,442 ball crops + 1,105 ball-free crops at native 640 px; YOLO26l fine-tuned 40 epochs.
self_trained_detector_round1.interpretation: More precise on this camera but almost never fires inside real gaps, indicating the ball is mostly not visible as a ball there; many generic gap detections are likely false. Round 2 not pursued.

candidates_not_promoted.observations: artifacts/video_gap_fill_observations.json (ignored; generated by session tooling, not yet a repository command)

decision: Not promoted (decided while the user was away): using video changes the tracking-only compliance class; possession evidence is teacher-based (circular); real-gap fills are edge extensions affecting 1.8-1.9% of graded frames. Working default unchanged. contact_carry_include_video_ball added as an off-by-default decoder flag.
not_started: Physics-and-player gap tracker: without visual support inside gap interiors it would infer touches without evidence (adversarial review issue 3).
